problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y(3\sqrt{x}+2),\,y(0)=2
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y(1),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y(1)≈{{field-1}}
$$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-0=1.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y(3\sqrt{x}+2)+{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,y(3\sqrt{x}+2)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}\,y(3\sqrt{x}+2)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}y(3\sqrt{x}+4)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2) & =\frac{1}{2}y(3\sqrt{x}+4) \\ \frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}(-3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}) & =\frac{1}{2}y(3\sqrt{x}+4) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =-\frac{y(3\sqrt{x}+4)}{3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=0+1=1.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =-\frac{y(3\sqrt{x}+4)}{3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}} \\  & =-\frac{2(3\sqrt{0}+4)}{3\sqrt{1}} \\  & =-\frac{8}{3} \\  & ≈-2.67.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(1)≈-2.67.$
